rows.description: The toddler runs, clings, smiles or bursts into tears at reunion: relief that the safe person is back. Caregiver should kneel, hold and say I am here, giving time before the next activity.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, indifference
related mind states: affection, relief, trust

rows.description: After a long day away the child follows father everywhere and wails if he steps out of sight. It is normal need to refill security, not spoiling. Give short, full-attention time before chores.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, indifference

rows.description: A tired parent who comes home glued to the phone gives the child no eye contact, so the child escalates with whining or mess to be noticed. A few minutes of warm, undivided attention prevents this.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence
related mind states: tiredness

rows.description: Around 1 to 2 the child hides behind the parent and stares, because unfamiliar faces feel risky. Wise adults let the child warm up from the parent's lap and never push or force a hug.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, curiosity
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: affection, anger, fear

rows.description: Once the parent looks relaxed, the toddler peeks, waves or offers a toy: safety is read from the parent's face. Caregivers show calm, let the child approach at own pace, and praise gently.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fear
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: curiosity, calm, trust

rows.description: When a relative demands a kiss or a lift and laughs at the child's refusal, the child feels her no does not count. Parents should back the child politely: she can wave or say namaste instead.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, fear
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: amusement

rows.description: The older child feels the baby gets everything and grabs to test whether he still matters. Parents should give one-on-one time and separate turns, not shame him as selfish.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, protectiveness
related mind states: shame, jealousy

rows.description: The small one clutches the toy and screams, having no words for mine. Caregivers should step in gently, name the feeling, and offer another turn rather than forcing sharing at once.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, jealousy

rows.description: Sometimes the older toddler hands a toy over to the crying baby and pats him: early empathy. Caregivers should notice and warmly name it, without demanding it every time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, jealousy, protectiveness
related mind states: affection, sadness, empathy

rows.description: The older toddler hits, whines or asks to be carried, wanting to know if there is still room for him. Wise parents reserve a little daily special time and let him help in small ways.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence
